Below is a high-level, professional survey of where and how to deploy surveillance in an Airbnb or similar short-term rental so as to maximize safety, deter vandalism/theft and preserve guest comfort and privacy.  Before installing any cameras, always:  
•  Review local/state laws and Airbnb (or platform) policies regarding tenant/guest notification and permitted camera locations.  
•  Disclose in your listing and via a visible notice on-site exactly where cameras are located and what they cover.  
•  Never install any recording device in private areas (bedrooms, bathrooms, changing areas).  

1.   Exterior Entry Points  
     •  Front door. A doorbell camera (e.g. 1080p Wi-Fi model with two-way audio) mounted at 7–8 ft covers anyone approaching or knocking, deters porch-piracy and records package drop-offs.  
     •  Rear/side doors or ground-level windows. Use small turret or bullet cameras with a 90°–120° field of view, installed under eaves or on window-overhangs.  
     •  Driveway/parking area. A weatherproof, wide-angle or multi-lens camera mounted on the garage façade or a lamp post can monitor vehicles and comings-and-goings.  

2.   Interior Common Areas  
     •  Living room. Place a discreet dome or cube camera high in a corner, tilted downward to capture the main seating and entry from the hall. At 12–15 ft up you get an unobstructed view without being eye-level.  
     •  Hallways/corridors. A narrow-field or varifocal lens camera centrally mounted in a hallway ceiling junction box will pick up foot traffic between rooms but will not invade bedrooms.  
     •  Kitchen/dining. If this is your primary communal zone, a recessed-look ceiling camera above the table or right inside the threshold can deter misuse of appliances, evidence spills or vandalism.  

3.   Discreet Integration Strategies  
     •  Smoke‐alarm housings or in-ceiling plenum fixtures (purpose-built “camera cans”). These blend in yet remain visible enough to meet most transparency laws.  
     •  Wall clocks or shelf-decor cameras. If you choose a stylized enclosure, keep it in plain sight—hidden cameras are often illegal and erode guest trust.  
     •  Wireless/Battery-powered options. Great for cluster zones or temporary placements; avoid exposed wiring.  

4.   Coverage Optimization  
     •  Overlap fields of view by ~10–15% from adjacent cameras to eliminate blind spots.  
     •  Opt for 1080p or 4K resolution and wide dynamic-range models to handle backlighting near windows.  
     •  Use pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) in larger spaces or parking areas—these can sweep predefined “patrol” paths on a schedule.  
     •  Enable motion detection alerts and privacy–masking (to blackout portions of the scene such as neighbors’ windows).  

5.   Data Security & Guest Comfort  
     •  Encrypt video at rest and in transit (WPA3 or WPA2-Enterprise Wi-Fi, or PoE over a VLAN).  
     •  Store footage on a secure, access-controlled cloud or local NVR with automatic overwrite after 14–30 days.  
     •  Publish clear “CCTV in operation” signage at main entrances, and include a “Privacy & Security” section in your digital welcome guide.  

6.   Respecting Guest Privacy  
     •  Explicitly exclude bedrooms, bathrooms, hot tubs and any private retreat areas from surveillance.  
     •  Limit audio recording (in some jurisdictions it’s prohibited) or disable it entirely.  
     •  Make camera locations and policies part of your booking confirmation so guests have no surprises.  

By combining well-positioned, visible cameras in all shared and exterior zones with robust data-security practices and full transparency, you create a safe environment that deters theft or property damage without undermining the trust and comfort of your guests.
